label: copy-phase input f whose next copied token is p (or f)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely (95% of mass) when the fed-back input is f (the rest on input p). It is a bigram feature: strongest when the model has just read f and must output p, i.e. the original contained "f p" (out_tok p carries ~69% of mass; top activations are "f p p" sequences, with an extra boost when the next output is also p). Weaker activation when the original bigram is "f f" (~18% of mass), and small activations for f followed by q, z, 3, etc. or input p followed by p. It barely fires at recall_idx 0-1 (f as the first original token). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and does not fire on most copy-phase f inputs followed by other tokens. Predicate (f then p/f, recall_idx>=2) gets dev F1 0.67, mass recall 0.80; the f->p clause alone has precision 0.85 but recall 0.39.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=f (+8.06), in_tok=f (+4.82), phase=2 & out_tok=p (+4.26), phase=2 & in_tok=p (+4.21), out_tok=p (+4.10), next_out=p (+3.93). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.91), out_tok=l (-2.51), next_out=e (-1.98), to_go=6 (-1.96).
